title: SDK credential handoff patterns, SSO token refresh, and secret safety guidance
text:
SDK credential handoff patterns, SSO token refresh, and secret safety guidance

description:
Goal: Define concrete, cross-language SDK patterns for handling credentials safely and ergonomically. This ticket collates best practices for API keys, short-lived SSO tokens, rotation workflows, streaming-auth scenarios, and local-dev ergonomics for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Motivation: customers integrating Redwood into long-lived services and interactive clients face subtle pitfalls: leaked secrets in logs, uncoordinated rotation causing 500s, streaming connections using stale tokens, and poor developer ergonomics for enterprise SSO. Deliverables: 1) a spec for SDK-level token/provider interfaces; 2) reference implementations (Python/TS/Go) showing token refresh, jitter, grace windows, and fallbacks; 3) a short 'do not log' guidance and local dev helper CLI usage; 4) tests and CI checks to prevent regressions.

acceptance_criteria:
SDKs expose a minimal token-provider interface that supports synchronous & async refresh in each language
Short-lived tokens (SSO) are refreshed proactively with configurable thresholds and jitter; reference implementations pass unit tests for refresh race conditions
Streaming APIs (server-sent events / web sockets / HTTP2) are documented with step-by-step token rotation patterns and sample code
Documentation includes local-dev secure defaults and an optional keyring/OS credential helper for storing secrets
Security review sign-off completed and a checklist added to the SDK repo to block merges that print secrets in logs

steps:
Draft token-provider interface: methods, expected semantics, and error surfacing for Python/TS/Go
Implement reference provider in each SDK that supports: initial load (env/credential file), on-demand refresh, background proactive refresh with jitter, and atomic swap on refresh success
Add streaming helper that demonstrates: attaching a short-lived Authorization header, re-auth handshake pattern for long-lived connections, and reconnection backoff with preserved progress tokens
Create local dev CLI guidance: recommended env var names, ephemeral file approach, and integration point with redwood-login (or similar) that writes to OS keyring
Write unit and integration tests for refresh races, network failure during refresh, token expiry edge cases, and CI lint rule to detect logging of credential-like strings
Produce docs + code samples for embedded enterprise flows: service-to-service rotation, customer KMS-signed tokens, and SSO refresh with PKCE examples
Run security review and iterate on any hardening recommendations (e.g., avoid in-memory long-lived caches for secrets, use zeroed buffers where applicable)

comments:
2026-03-10 Maya Patel: Initial draft. Observed customer incident where long-lived streaming client failed after SSO token rotation — need a canonical reconnection/refresh pattern.
2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Proposed token-provider API sketch attached in related_links. Prefer non-breaking adapter so existing SDK users can opt-in.
2026-03-12 Security: request for explicit guidance on telemetry — confirm we redact any Authorization headers in logs and mask keys in CLI output.
2026-03-12 Maya Patel: Will include CI rule using repo grep pre-commit hook + test that simulates token rotation mid-stream. Planning to land minimal provider interface in a feature flag for SDK v-next.
